title: Severe Frame Drops/Freezing with High Polling Rate Mouse (MCHOSE L7 PRO at 4000Hz/8000Hz) - Input Accumulation Fails
body:
### Tested versions

Godot 4.5 / Godot 4.6 (Testing branches)

### System information

OS: Windows 11 / Windows 10 Mouse: MCHOSE L7 PRO (Running at 4000Hz / 8000Hz polling rate via official driver)

### Issue description

When using a high polling rate mouse (4000Hz or 8000Hz), moving the mouse quickly causes massive CPU spikes and severe frame drops, sometimes completely freezing the main thread.

I initially encountered this while developing my 2D game BOP&POP, where GUI node traversal was suspected. However, the exact same issue persists even in a completely empty project.

Important Note: I have already tried all standard workarounds, but none resolved the underlying stutter:

Input.use_accumulated_input = true is enabled.

Agile Event Flushing is disabled in Project Settings.

physics_object_picking is set to false.

V-Sync is disabled and FPS is capped to monitor refresh rate.

Even setting Input.set_deferred("mouse_mode", Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED) or explicitly calling get_viewport().set_input_as_handled() in _input() to manually throttle the events does not fix it.

It appears the bottleneck is entirely at the OS message pump level (WM_INPUT/Message Queue) or DisplayServer before it even reaches the GDScript input callbacks. The engine struggles to handle the sheer volume of hardware interrupts from modern 8K mice.

Steps to reproduce:

Set the physical mouse polling rate to 4000Hz or 8000Hz via its driver software.

Open the attached empty minimal reproduction project.

Run the project and move the mouse rapidly across the screen.

Observe the severe FPS drop and frame time spikes in the profiler.
